speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The Members asked about two separate cases of fraudulent claims.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The fraudulent claims were made by individuals who did not attend any training but falsely claimed to have done so.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: They acted largely on their own accord, prompted by a viral WhatsApp message.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As of December, over 90% of these individuals have either made full payment or have made arrangements for instalment payments.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Those who did not respond will be blacklisted for all future SkillsFuture grant claims until they have repaid.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We will also not rule out further legal and enforcement actions.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Arising from that episode, SkillsFuture Singapore (SSG) has reviewed the claims processes for SkillsFuture Credit.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Individuals can no longer be directly reimbursed by SSG for use of SkillsFuture Credit.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Instead, payments will be made to training providers, who then reduce the course fees chargeable accordingly.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: This arrangement has significantly reduced the risk of false claims under SkillsFuture Credit.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: At the same time, the claim process is still convenient and easy and has not affected the number of individuals using their SkillsFuture Credit every month.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It did not involve SkillsFuture Credit or new SkillsFuture programmes.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Instead, the fraudulent claims were for training grants drawn from the Skills Development Fund (SDF).

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: SDF was established in 1979 to support the training and retraining of workers and workforce upgrading programmes and is built up through levies collected from employers.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It is, therefore, a scheme that has been around for many years.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: From its preliminary investigations, the Police believe that a criminal syndicate was behind this.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The syndicate operated an organised network that utilised business entities, comprising employer companies and training providers to submit fraudulent claims.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Central Provident Fund documents provided by the syndicate listed employees that the Police believe were fictitious.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In short, this appears to be an elaborate and conscious effort.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: These fraudulent claims were made in 2017, with the majority being made in October.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: When these irregular claims were detected, SSG immediately suspended all payments of grants to the relevant business entities and reported the case to the Police.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Five persons have been charged with various offences, such as engaging in a conspiracy to submit forged documents and concealing the benefits from criminal conduct.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As investigations are ongoing, I am unable to disclose more details about the case.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But what is clear is that this case involves fraudulent claims amounting to a large quantum.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: This should not have been allowed to happen.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: While we cannot always prevent all forms of fraudulent activities, SSG should have detected this case much earlier, especially when it was so egregious and the amounts involved were so large.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: SSG's priorities are as follows: firstly, work with the enforcement agencies on the current prosecution to ensure that any perpetrators will face the full consequences of the law; secondly, systematically plough through other claims it has received over the past year.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And thankfully, so far, there is no evidence of other cases of a similar nature.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Thirdly and very urgently, improve the system of fraud detection, checks and audits.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: SSG has formed an Interagency Process Review Task Force, overseen by its Board, and comprising members from SSG management, the Accountant-General’s Department, Commercial Affairs Department and the Ministry of Education (MOE).

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The task force is conducting a thorough review of how the fraudulent cases happened and will evaluate the current fraud detection system and make recommendations to improve the system.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Specifically, I have directed SSG to strengthen its fraud detection system through data analytics.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Fraudsters, who are going all out to cheat, are getting more sophisticated and their plans more elaborate.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: SSG's detection system must improve and become more sophisticated, too.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Through appropriate use of data analytics and drawing on data across Government agencies, we can better detect false claims without significantly affecting genuine employers applying for training grants to upgrade the skills of their workers.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: SSG is currently getting help from both private sector consultants and Government Technology Agency (GovTech) to get this done.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It has restructured and strengthened the fraud detection and audit team.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: SSG has started implementing some of the measures manually and will progressively automate and systematise them.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: By the third quarter of this year, we will have a good and effective data analytics system in place.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In response to Mr Zaqy Mohamad's question, as of now, no staff member has been disciplined or suspended arising from the latest fraud case as there has been no evidence of wrongdoing by any staff member thus far.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But SSG will take necessary management measures to remedy this weakness in fraud detection capability.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We must also take the real culprits to task, send a strong deterrent signal, so that SkillsFuture continues to serve the working people of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We cannot afford a repeat of fraudulent claims of such egregious nature and of such scale.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: The Minister agrees that because of the large amount of public funds involved, we need measures to prevent such occurrences from happening in the future.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Will the Ministry consider raising the bar or, in fact, having greater sanctions and harsher penalties in the review for the SDF Levy Act as well as related legislation involving public funds?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: This will clearly come under the Penal Code.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: When we set up SSG, we enacted the SSG Act.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But for cases, such as this, of such an egregious nature will have to come under the Penal Code.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I have received feedback from residents that, very often, they were falsely told that SkillsFuture Credit will expire, for example, while some are being told that they would need further courses in order for their certificate to be valid.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: For example, is there a hotline set up for residents to report such service providers?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We will definitely consider having such a hotline.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I believe a hotline to SSG does exist, but we probably have to make it more widely known.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The Member can assure her residents that SkillsFuture Credit does not expire.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I welcome the Minister's approach and strategies to combat such scams in the future.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Bearing in mind that this may also mean tightening of the processes, firstly, how would SSG balance not having to make it more onerous for employers to claim and, secondly, given that $40 million was involved in the scams, how does it affect the performance and results that SkillsFuture had earlier reported?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In any case, training numbers are not really the full outcome of what SkillsFuture is trying to achieve.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We work closely with the Ministry of Manpower.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The Adapt and Grow numbers drawing on SkillsFuture funding and programmes are much more important.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Thus, outcomes are one thing, key performance indicators are one thing, but understand the spirit of what we are trying to do and the real ground impact of what we want to do.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The natural instinct is to think, "Because this thing happened, let us double-check everything and let us check a huge number" but this will impede the whole system.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: That is when genuine employers who want to train their workers will get affected.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But we do not have to do that and, if we do that, we will end up putting out efforts in the wrong areas.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: What we want to do is, through data analytics, work out the pattern of cheating and then we can detect them much better.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: That pattern of detection of cheating has to keep on evolving because they are evolving, too.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: If we can do that well – and we must do that well – we will not over burden employers.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We can improve the audit and fraud detection system while not over-burdening employers.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: First, will GovTech be involved in the move to use data analytics to prevent fraudulent claims and, secondly, what are the terms of reference for the Interagency Task Force and will they be making their findings public?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The answer to the first question is yes, GovTech is involved.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Beyond GovTech, we are also inviting private sector expertise to help us in this work.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: If the Member files a question, I will be happy to report on the findings of the task force.
